title: Showmob roadmap: the next three phases from conversation to preserved learning
summary: Phase 1's first milestone is on the board. What comes next: sizing sections on purpose, users without a login wall, and expansion requests with graded verdicts.

blocks.title: The next three phases
blocks.body: The numbered plan has eight phases. Phase 1's first milestone is real: artifacts now save to a database as immutable revisions, proven end to end. This page is the reflective version of what comes after - sizing, then people, then requests - and why that order.

items.label: In flight - revisions save and read back, renderer still reads repo JSON
Grading-night pages in build - the first big content experiment

blocks.heading: The next three at a glance

items.title: Size sections on purpose
items.detail: A thinking structure for how big a section or artifact should be - the rubric that turns taste into something checkable.

items.title: Users without a login wall
items.detail: Dev-mode auto-admin for builders, plus simulated commenters and requesters, so multi-user behavior gets rehearsed before identity is real.

items.title: Expansion requests
items.detail: A viewer asks for more on a subject; an agent answers with a graded verdict. The first write that is not the builder's own.

blocks.heading: Phase 2 - size sections on purpose
blocks.body: Today, density is instinct. One page gets twenty-two blocks because the subject earned them; another gets three because it earned three, and nobody wrote down why. Phase 2 writes it down: a working structure that maps how developed an idea is to how much interface it deserves. A weak concept earns a sentence and a needs-evidence marker, not a dashboard. A mature one earns sections, visuals, and links. The output is not a style guide to obey; it is a vocabulary for arguing about size.

blocks.title: Grading night is Phase 2's field test
blocks.body: The hundred pages being built right now are the first real data for that rubric. Each one has a target density - microscopic through extreme - and a person about to grade whether the size fit the idea. The grades are the ground truth Phase 2 gets written from.

items.label: A written sizing structure exists
items.detail: Short enough to hold in your head; honest about edge cases.

items.label: Two existing pages have been re-sized against it
items.detail: One that shrinks, one that grows - proving the rubric moves both directions.

items.label: New pages carry a size rationale in their plan note
items.detail: One sentence: why this page is this big.

blocks.heading: Phase 3 - users without a login wall
blocks.body: Real identity is Phase 4-and-later work, but multi-user behavior cannot wait for it. Phase 3 fakes the crowd honestly: the builder runs as auto-admin in dev, and simulated commenters and requesters leave their marks. That is enough to answer the questions identity would complicate - where do requests live, what does a comment do to a page, who sees what in the list - without standing up an auth system to learn them.

items.label: A simulated requester can leave a request against a page
items.detail: Stored, listed, and attributable to the simulation - not confused with a real person.

items.label: The builder can answer, defer, or decline it in dev mode
items.detail: The triage loop exists before the users do.

items.label: Nothing simulated renders as if a real human said it
items.detail: Provenance stays honest end to end.

blocks.heading: Phase 4 - expansion requests
blocks.body: This is the first write to the system that is not the builder's own hand. A reader asks for more on a subject - go deeper, add the example, cover the exception - and an agent answers with a graded verdict: expand, defer, or decline, with reasons. The verdict matters as much as the expansion. A page that grows on every ask becomes a pile; the graded verdict is what keeps growth honest.

items.label: A request can travel from reader to verdict without chat
items.detail: The system carries it, not a message thread.

items.label: An accepted expansion lands as a new revision
items.detail: Immutable history - the page grows by appending, never by overwriting.

items.label: Declines explain themselves
items.detail: A no with reasons teaches the next request; a silent no teaches nothing.

blocks.heading: The loop these three phases serve

nodes.title: Conversation
nodes.detail: An idea starts as ordinary talk.

nodes.title: Artifact
nodes.detail: The idea gets composed as portable JSON.

nodes.title: Presentation
nodes.detail: Someone opens the artifact as a room and walks it.

nodes.title: Interaction
nodes.detail: Questions, requests, and notes land against the page.

nodes.title: Preserved learning
nodes.detail: What the room captured is kept, not lost when the tab closes.

nodes.title: Enriched artifact
nodes.detail: Approved follow-ups fold back into the page's series as new revisions.

blocks.heading: Why sizing comes before people
blocks.body: Tempting as it is to build the social layer first, requests about badly-sized pages just make more badly-sized pages. Phase 2 gives the system a sense of proportion; Phase 3 rehearses the crowd; Phase 4 lets the crowd actually tug on the content. By the time preserved learning arrives in earnest, the system already knows how big an answer should be.
